The SpyPopen records only constructor kwargs; the stdin payload goes to `proc.communicate(input, ...)` (src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:309), which the test never captures or checks.
The non-bounded sibling test does pin the exact output: `assert out.stdout == expected`, where expected is git's hash of b"a\nb\n".

The other new tests in the same file fake the external boundary instead (`gitutil.subprocess.run` / `gitutil.subprocess.Popen`).
advisory.finding: The bounded-path test never checks the bytes fed to git's stdin or the resulting hash. It asserts only that Popen got `text=False` and that the hash is 40 characters long, so it would stay green if the bounded path encoded the text wrongly (for example by putting `\r\n` back or using another codec).
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute `expected = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "hash-object", "--stdin"], input=b"a\nb\n", capture_output=True).stdout.decode()` with the real subprocess.run before patching, then `assert out.stdout == expected`.

dropped.finding: The two new `-text` attributes for the SHA-256-pinned vendored files have no attribute-level test on the Linux gate, so deleting or mistyping them leaves every gating test green. The only thing that would notice is the Windows sweep, which runs on schedule, is advisory and uses continue-on-error.
scenarios: Someone deletes the new `-text` lines or renames `.github/schemas/gitlab-ci.schema.json` without updating .gitattributes. Every PR gate stays green, and the regression shows up only as a red result on a later scheduled Windows sweep that does not block merges.
